name: libyojimbo
desc: Secure client/server network protocol library for multiplayer games
why: A secure client/server protocol library from game networking, a door into reliable UDP and encrypted transport worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: yojimbo is a network library for client/server games, written in C++. It gives a game a secure connection layer over UDP: clients authenticate with connect tokens, and packets are encrypted and signed. On top of that it offers unreliable-unordered messages for time-sensitive data, reliable-ordered messages, and per-connection stats (latency, jitter, packet loss, bandwidth). The README frames it as a library you link into a C++ game engine, not a standalone program.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it is "designed around the networking requirements of competitive multiplayer games like first person shooters" and that "if you have a game engine written in C++ and you want to network your game, yojimbo is a really good choice."
brief.how_it_works: Authentication uses connect tokens based on the netcode standard, and packets are encrypted and signed before being sent over UDP. Large payloads are split by packet fragmentation and reassembled on receipt. Reliable-ordered messages are resent aggressively until acknowledged, while unreliable-unordered messages are sent without that guarantee. The README also mentions a bitpacker and serialization system but does not explain its internals.

commands_seen.context: Source checkout command given in the README's Source Code section; the README points to releases as an alternative to cloning.

brief.install_notes: No build or install commands appear in the README. It refers to CONTRIBUTING.md for how to build and test, which I did not fetch. Installation is by cloning the repository or downloading a release archive from GitHub. Using it requires that the client and server share the same ClientServerConfig, channels and message factory, and that all yojimbo calls run on one thread.
brief.standout: It is built on a small family of open libraries from the same author (netcode for the connection and token layer, reliable for reliable messaging, serialize for serialization), and the README asks that product credits name all four together. Its design is explicit about its limits, aimed at games with 100 players or fewer.
brief.status: Maintained, with limited evidence. The README has a CI badge and calls the library "stable and production ready." It links to a releases page and a SECURITY.md policy. I did not see a release date or last-commit date, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README says it is designed for games with 100 players or fewer. Client and server must use identical configuration, and keeping them in sync is the developer's job. It is single-threaded; all calls must come from one thread. It is C++ only and targets game engines. It bundles libsodium and tlsf, whose own licenses apply. The license is BSD 3-Clause, but the README asks that product credits name yojimbo, netcode, reliable and serialize; this is a request, not a license requirement. The README also asks for Patreon support.
